task.description: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-001b.md independently. Run WF-02 Step 1b's gate: (a) every acceptance criterion has a corresponding design element, no TBD/deferral language outside the explicitly-labeled open-questions section; (b) props/types (here: message-catalog key names, not component props, since this requirement adds no new component) fully specified; (c) no color/spacing/token violation — this requirement touches no CSS, so this check is trivially satisfied, confirm the design doesn't introduce any; (d) no .tsx implementation code present. The design makes several judgment calls you must specifically evaluate: (1) all 12 components correctly identified as Server Components using getTranslations — verify by reading the actual files' first lines yourself; (2) the flat-indexed-key vs JSON-array-value decision for the 6 repeated-shape arrays (Events.TALKS, MapSection.CHAPTERS, Metrics.METRICS, Partners.PARTNERS, Streams.STREAMS, Team.TEAM) — the design picked flat indexed keys and flagged it as open question 4 needing your confirmation; give an actual verdict, don't just note it's flagged. (3) The empty-array-copy pitfall audit (content_ba_guide.md §5) — verify the design's claim that none of the 12 components uses array.join()-into-a-sentence by checking the actual source yourself. Six open questions are listed (brand-name extraction scope, <em>-emphasis handling, Telegram-handle splitting, flat-key-vs-array choice, MapSection aria-label desync, nav anchor scope) — for each, decide whether it's a legitimate implementation-time judgment call to leave for FRONTEND-DEV, or something that must be resolved before Step 2 can proceed sensibly.
acceptance_criteria: Checks a-d run against docs/agents/design/REQ-001b.md directly
Server/Client component classification independently verified against actual source files
A real verdict given on the flat-key-vs-JSON-array open question, not just acknowledgment that it's flagged
Each of the 6 open questions explicitly triaged: pass-through to FRONTEND-DEV, or blocking
